svg.aria-label: MAE and RMSE on the same errors Panel: Keep the predictions fixed Panel: Measure each miss Panel: Aggregate the same four errors Three small misses and a larger one Input: 0 to 4 Target: 0 to 9 Prediction (line): (0, 1); (4, 5) Observed (scatter): s1 S1 (1, 3); s2 S2 (2, 2); s3 S3 (3, 5); s4 S4 (4, 8) $e_1=1$: (1, 2) → (1, 3) $e_2=-1$: (2, 3) → (2, 2) $e_3=1$: (3, 4) → (3, 5) $e_4=3$: (4, 5) → (4, 8) Prediction is $\hat y=x+1$. A residual is actual minus predicted: $e=y-\hat y$. The line is the same for all four samples. One row per residual Error | Abs. | Square S1: 1 | 1 | 1 S2: -1 | 1 | 1 S3: 1 | 1 | 1 S4: 3 | 3 | 9 S4: highlighted row Absolute errors total 6. Squared errors total 12. Taking magnitudes or squares prevents opposite signs from cancelling. Average over all four samples Calculation | Result MAE: $6/4$ | 1.500 MSE: $12/4$ | 3.000 RMSE: $\sqrt{12/4}$ | 1.732 MAE and RMSE use target units; MSE uses squared units. Every sample has equal weight. Displayed results are rounded. The largest miss supplies half the total absolute error and three quarters of the total squared error. Squaring gives it more influence.
